volumes.notes: Key finding: the served loci are NOT raw PG 158 column numbers. Each served locus L holds the Greek of one real Migne column pair, real_col = 2*(L-35) (pair 2L-71/2L-70). This mapping was verified at 20+ independent points against Migne's own conspectus (Documenta Catholica Omnia, 'PG Volumen 158 Rerum Conspectus Pro Columnis Ordinatus'): Annales Pars I col 27=served 49, Pars II 231=151, Pars III 385=228, Pars IV 465=268, Epistolae 647=359 with per-letter headers matching (659=365, 715=393, 721=396, 727=399, 782=426, 793=432, 799=435, 811=441, 817=444, 831=451, 838=454, 845=458, 897=484, 899=485, 913=492, 921=496, 927=499, 951=511), Joannes Diaconus 959=515, Esaias Cyprius 971=521, Hilario 977=524, Argyropulus 991=531, Agallianus 1011=541, Josephus patriarcha 1051=561, Job 1053=562, Anonymus 1077=574. Any split script should carry both the served locus and the reconstructed real column. Credited work tlg3047.002 (Annales lectiones variae) is NOT identifiable in the served text: it is keyed to Bekker pages, and the PG 'Glycanorum Annalium continuatio' (real cols 623-646) falls in the missing served rows 348-358; do not assign it a column range. Boundary caveats: served columns are shared at three seams (561 holds Agallianus end + Josephus confessio; 562 holds the Josephi epitaphium caption + Job incipit; 539 holds Argyropulus chapters ια-ιβ and, per the conspectus, the start of his Epistola ad Dominicum at real 1007, which is not visibly present). Confidence 'high': every start boundary has a title line or incipit in the served text except Argyropulus at 531, which has a chapter-numbered incipit naming the addressee (megas doux) plus the conspectus column match and Agallianos' back-reference.
